# Independent mathematical audit — SCOPE-20260914-041

Disposition: **failed**.

## Correctness
**PASS** — Wiedmer proves PSO(A_Gamma'(Lambda)) is isomorphic to A_Lambda and finite index in Out(A_Gamma'(Lambda)), with quotient generated by vertex inversions and isomorphic to an elementary 2-group. If Out is acylindrically hyperbolic, its infinite finite-index normal PSO subgroup is s-normal, so Osin's theorem forces PSO to be acylindrically hyperbolic; the standard RAAG criterion gives the necessity. For edgeless Lambda, PSO=F_n is finite index, hence Out is virtually nonabelian free. I also rebuilt Gamma'(Lambda) independently with a plain adjacency implementation and reproduced the stated SIL counts and joined-outside property on the listed test graphs.

## Originality
**PASS** — The necessity and edgeless sufficiency are direct corollaries of published results and are therefore not novel by themselves. The only best-of-knowledge non-covered component is the explicit finite SIL census/placement on the 12 listed Lambda types; targeted Resultary search found no prior table.

### Equivalent formulations
That main implication is already mechanically contained in general theorems, so it contributes no originality; the census is a separate finite statement.

### Broader coverage
These sources broadly cover parts (a)-(b), while the finite 12-type SIL table is not supplied there.

### Exact database or table
This supports originality only of the finite census, not of the theorem-level implications.

### Claim versus prior implication
The final composite claim contains prior-implied and newly computed components; originality is credited only to the latter.

### Source inspections
- **Right-angled Artin groups as finite-index subgroups of their outer automorphism groups** (https://doi.org/10.1112/blms.12954): covers finite-index PSO and elementary 2-group quotient. Corollary 3.8 identifies Out/PSO with the inversion subgroup quotient after graph automorphisms vanish.
- **Acylindrically hyperbolic groups** (https://doi.org/10.1090/tran/6343): covers s-normal inheritance. An s-normal subgroup of an acylindrically hyperbolic group is acylindrically hyperbolic under the relevant infinite condition.

## Scientific value
**FAIL** — The theorem-level necessity and edgeless sufficiency are routine consequences of published finite-index and s-normal results. The remaining original material is a 12-instance small-graph census plus an open-problem diagnosis; it does not establish a general regime theorem, a decisive boundary, or another independently motivated exact invariant sufficient to clear the value bar.

## Residual risks
